Header:
Date: 2027-06-30
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~61 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonah Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Stellarex Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Platform), Priya Singh (Security)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood Optimize recommendations focused on batching and prefix/KV caching for Stellarex's payments chat logs; discussed cost model assumptions, expected hit rates, tradeoffs between latency and token unit cost, and pilot/benchmark next steps.

Topics:
- Current stack and traffic profile (Alicia)
- Batching strategies and continuous batching behavior (Jonah)
- Prefix vs KV cache use cases and hit-rate modeling (Jonah/Maya)
- Cost model: tokens saved vs latency impact (Maya)
- Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs private (Priya/Tom)
- Next steps: benchmark, pricing, security docs

Action items (captured in metadata above) and links:
- Shared deck: https://redwood.app/decks/optimize-batching-kv-stellarex (shared during call)
- Benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/stellarex-kv-24h

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Jonah our SE. Um Alicia, Tom, Priya, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Alicia: Yeah thanks Maya, excited to go through optimizations, we have pretty high qps during peak hours and the token bill has been creeping up.
[00:18] Jonah: Cool, quick agenda: we'll walk through batching fundamentals, then prefix vs KV cache recommendations, and then a cost model with example numbers. We'll leave time for questions.
[00:30] Tom: Sounds good, hi all.
[00:34] Priya: Hi, quick note from security: we'll need SOC2 and KMS details after the demo.
[00:39] Maya: Yep we'll share those, Priya, we'll add the compliance pack to the sheet.

[00:45] Jonah: Ok starting with batching: Redwood's runtime does continuous batching at the request layer. Practically that means we can lower per-token cost by grouping short requests into micro-batches without adding much tail latency. For your chat endpoint, we saw median request length ~120 tokens and p95 ~900 on sample. If you enable a 50ms batching window you can typically be batching 8-12 requests on our hosted fleet at your projected throughput which saves ~18-22% per-token cost on small models, more on higher-throughput models.
[01:25] Alicia: That makes sense, our main concern is p95 latency. If we batch more are we going to blow out p95?
[01:32] Jonah: Good question — batching tradeoff is added queueing time. Redwood's recommendation is to use adaptive batching: small fixed window (30-70ms) with size caps. For interactive chat we usually recommend 50ms max window to keep added latency within 50-80ms while still getting meaningful batching gains. Also note we do token-aware batching so longer requests don't block small ones too long.
[02:05] Tom: Token-aware batching — can you explain?
[02:08] Jonah: Sure. We build batches by combining requests but we prefer to keep the compute bound per batch below a configured token budget so a single 2k-token request doesn't delay a bunch of 50-token requests. We can set a token budget per batch for your workload — e.g., 4k tokens — and the batching runtime will flush earlier if budget hits. That's configurable per-route in the console.

[02:40] Jonah: Next, prefix vs KV cache. Two different patterns: prefix or prefix caching is good when you have repeated leading context — say a system prompt or user profile — that is identical across requests. KV cache refers to key-value (kv) caching of past model activations for autoregressive decoding — that helps when you have long histories where the KV cache speeds up repeated next-token generation. They are complementary.
[03:05] Alicia: For us, we have a fairly stable system prompt and template plus conversation history that often repeats small snippets. Which would get us more wins?
[03:14] Jonah: Likely both: prefix caching will eliminate the cost of re-encoding the system prompt each time. If your prompt is 250 tokens and repeated for 100k daily calls that's a big saving. KV cache helps with long histories: if users re-open chats and the prior tokens are cached you'll avoid recomputing key/value matrices which reduces GPU time per-token during generation.

[03:40] Maya: We'll show a simple cost model. Assumptions: baseline hosted model cost (on our open model profile) at 0.6ms per token on our infra and unit compute cost of $0.00012 per token (example numbers), average request 120 tokens input + 80 tokens generation = 200 tokens. Without caching or batching, 1M requests = 200M tokens => $24,000/month. With batching and prefix cache we estimate token savings and compute reduction.
[04:20] Jonah: Example scenario A: 50ms batching window achieves 20% token-cost reduction due to better packing and lower overhead, prefix cache hits 60% of requests (system prompt reused), KV cache hit for reopened sessions about 25% of generations. Combined effect reduces effective billed tokens by ~40% and compute time by ~35% depending on hit rates, bringing 1M requests cost from $24k to ~ $14k - $16k.
[05:02] Alicia: Those are promising. How sensitive is that to hit rates?
[05:06] Jonah: Very. If prefix hit drops to 30% the combined savings fall to ~22-25%. We usually recommend instrumenting with a sample run to measure real hit rates; Redwood's console can ingest logs and estimate hit potential.

[05:22] Tom: For the KV cache, what's the memory footprint? We can't blow up inference nodes.
[05:27] Jonah: KV cache size depends on model hidden size and sequence length. For a 16k context model and typical hidden dims, caching a 2K-token history per session might be ~30-60MB per active session depending on quantization. Redwood's Dedicated pools allow you to reserve capacity and we have eviction/pinning policies for long-running sessions. For your traffic profile we estimate 10-15k concurrent active KV sessions as peak which is within dedicated configuration but we'll size it during the PoC.
[06:00] Priya: On encryption — is the KV cache stored encrypted at rest? How about keys in memory?
[06:06] Maya: By default KV cache in our hosted offering is encrypted at rest and in transit; for Private we can integrate KMS/HSM. We'll include SOC2, KMS docs.

[06:18] Jonah: Back to cost model: we ran a micro-benchmark for a payments workload (similar to Stellarex sample) — raw numbers: baseline latency median 120ms, p95 450ms. With 50ms batching median increased to 145ms, p95 to 510ms; throughput improved and cost per generation dropped ~21%. With KV cache enabled for reopened sessions we saw generation time drop by ~30% for cached requests.
[06:52] Alicia: p95 bump is not ideal but might be acceptable. We need SLOs at 500ms p95.
[06:58] Jonah: Right — our adaptive batching keeps p95 usually within 10% of baseline for moderate windows; we can tune. Also you can set per-route SLO enforcement where Redwood will bypass batching for requests near SLO boundaries.

[07:15] Maya: One operational note: fallback policies. If a dedicated pool is saturated we'll route to a compatible hosted variant or a lower-precision quantized variant to keep tail latency bounded. That can change the quality slightly; we recommend running evals on your prompt set to measure quality delta.
[07:36] Alicia: How do you measure quality delta — is that automatic?
[07:40] Jonah: Redwood Optimize has a regression monitoring pipeline; you can attach a set of prompts and expected outputs, run A/B between baseline and quantized variants, and we report BLEU-like similarity and custom metrics. You can set alerts on regression.

[07:55] Tom: For dedicated vs hosted cost — can you send a sample pricing sheet? We need monthly committed price for dedicated with KV cache sizing.
[08:02] Maya: Yes — action item: we'll send the dedicated SKU pricing and a recommended commit range. We'll include burst options and autoscale policy pricing.

[08:10] Priya: Data residency — our EU customers require logs not to leave region. Can Redwood do region pinning for caching?
[08:18] Jonah: Yes. For Private or Dedicated in-region pools, KV cache and prefix cache can be pinned to region, and we provide audit logs. For hosted we also offer region controls per deployment. We'll follow up with the architecture doc.

[08:30] Maya: Quick pause — any questions on batching mechanics?
[08:33] Alicia: One more: if a user opens many concurrent short chats, could batching introduce head-of-line blocking?
[08:39] Jonah: That's why token-aware batching and request size caps matter. Also you can configure per-route concurrency limits so long requests are shunted to separate lanes. In practice we've seen minimal head-of-line issues with the defaults but we'll test with your workload.

[09:00] Jonah: Now recommendations specific to Stellarex:
- Start with hosted Optimize + prefix caching enabled for system prompts (low risk, high reward).
- Enable a conservative 40-50ms batching window with token budget 4k for chat route.
- Pilot KV cache on a subset of premium sessions (e.g., saved chats) where reopen rate is high; set eviction TTL 24h initially.
- Run a 24-72 hour benchmark to measure real prefix and KV hit rates; Redwood can run this with a sample trace.

[09:40] Alicia: Sounds good. For the pilot, what metrics should we watch?
[09:44] Jonah: Hit rates (prefix and KV), effective tokens per request, median and p95 latency, cost per 1k requests as reported in console, and quality/regression metrics for quantized fallbacks.

[09:58] Maya: We'll also provide an example cost sensitivity chart in the deck which shows cost vs prefix hit rate and batching window.

[10:06] Jonah: Example from the chart: at 60% prefix hit and 25% KV hit with 50ms batching you get ~38% token reduction; if prefix hit drops to 30% that falls to ~20%. We model both token-savings and compute-savings — the latter important for dedicated commitments.

[10:28] Tom: Any gotchas for our infra? We're mostly GCP-based and use VPC-SC for some services.
[10:33] Maya: For Private or Dedicated on GCP we integrate with customer VPCs; if you require VPC-SC compatibility we'll validate network flows. For hosted we do egress controls and limited IP ranges; we'll share the network diagram.

[10:45] Priya: A couple security Qs: SSO (SAML) for console, RBAC, audit log retention?
[10:50] Maya: All supported. We'll attach the security checklist; you can configure RBAC per-team and export audit logs to your SIEM.

[11:00] Alicia: Ok, timeline — we'd like to have a pilot by mid-July.
[11:03] Maya: Great, we'll target PoC scoping week of 7/12 and start benchmark earlier if you can share sample traffic.

[11:10] (group confirms dates)

- We'll send pricing, dedicated SKUs, SOC2/KMS docs (Maya)

- Alicia to share 7-day sample traffic and a couple representative prompt templates (Alicia)
